about.title: Holtville Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Holtville is a small place. With about 6,400 residents, public collision records for 2025 show a single injury crash, one person hurt and no traffic deaths. Those numbers are a relief, but they also mean that when a fatal loss does happen here, whether on 5th Street, Holt Avenue, Maple Avenue or Walnut Avenue, or in a field, a clinic or a workplace, nearly everyone in town feels it. Reported crashes in Holtville tend to cluster on Saturday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m., a reminder that these events often unfold during ordinary family time. A wrongful death claim under California law is a civil action, kept separate from any criminal case the district attorney may or may not pursue. It allows a spouse or domestic partner, children and, in some situations, other dependents or heirs to recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Holtville families with an independent attorney, for free, so the legal side does not fall on you alone.

items.question: Holtville had no traffic deaths in 2025. Does a wrongful death claim still apply to my situation?
items.answer: Yes. Wrongful death claims are not limited to car crashes, and low local crash numbers do not change your family's rights. If a death in or around Holtville was caused by negligence of any kind, including a workplace incident, medical error, defective product or unsafe property, the same California rules apply. An independent attorney can review the specific facts with you.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: The law gives first priority to the surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children of the person who died. If there are none, certain other dependents or heirs may be able to bring the claim. Because these rules are strict, it helps to have an attorney identify the proper parties before filing.

items.question: Is a wrongful death case the same as the criminal case against the person responsible?
items.answer: No, they are separate. A criminal case is brought by prosecutors and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by the family to recover losses such as funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of companionship and guidance. A civil claim can move forward whether or not criminal charges are filed.
